maker: Guido van Rossum, then the Python Software Foundation
summary: A general-purpose language built for readable code. Guido van Rossum started it as a holiday project at CWI in the Netherlands, and it grew into the most widely taught language and the main language of data science and machine learning.

icon.licence: CC0 1.0 (the mark itself belongs to its owner)

image.alt: Guido van Rossum, who created Python

events.note: Guido van Rossum starts writing Python at CWI as a successor to the ABC language.
Version 0.9.0 is posted to the alt.sources newsgroup.

events.label: Python 2.0
events.note: Adds list comprehensions and a cycle-detecting garbage collector.

events.label: Python 3
events.note: A clean-up release that breaks backward compatibility; the move from Python 2 takes twelve years.

events.label: Moves to GitHub
events.note: Development moves from a self-hosted Mercurial repository to GitHub.

events.label: BDFL steps down
events.note: Guido van Rossum steps down as "Benevolent Dictator for Life".

events.label: Steering Council
events.note: A five-member Steering Council elected by core developers takes over leadership.
